title: Waivers and category allowlist
description: <design>/waivers.json (scripts/CONTRACTS.md 5 and 6.2), read by rules/load.mjs loadAllowlists(). waivers: a tier-2 rule that fires passes tells.tier2 only with a waiver whose reason and evidence are non-empty and tied to research or the sponsor's real brand; a waiver citing a sponsor whose allowlist entry has claimed_as_mark true is refused by the checker (FD21). category: the category allowlist, a rule id plus the recorded reason the sponsor customers' category uses the pattern (rules builder's extension of 6.2). Exemptions are never by colour or by name alone. v1.1 (2026-10): waivers may also carry rule coverage.features, the owner's decision to keep listed feature rows off the page (coverage.mjs reads them).

rule.description: A rule id of rules/registry.json (tells), or, v1.1 (2026-10), the gate id coverage.features for an owner waiver that keeps a catalogue row off the page.

scope.description: What the waiver covers (v1.1 grammar, slop-check): '/route' (every finding on that route), '/route <css selector>' (the matched element or anything inside it), a bare CSS selector (every route), or a repo file path or glob with an optional ':line' (static findings). Never the whole site: empty, *, **, site, all, global, everywhere, html, :root, body, document, /*, /** and /**/* are refused. For rule coverage.features: the FR ids kept off the page.

evidence.description: Research finding ids, a sponsor allowlist entry or files that back the reason.

allOf.description: v1.1 (2026-10): a coverage.features waiver is the owner's written decision to keep feature rows off the page (BD-06, BF-07). scope lists the requirement ids (FR-003 or FR-003, FR-007), approved_by is owner (a research approval exempts nothing) and evidence is one non-empty string naming the decision record.

category.description: The sponsor customers' category, for example defi-lending.

reason.description: Why the category uses this pattern, measured on its human-designed exemplars.

source.description: The finding or pattern-ledger entry that records it.
